correctness.rationale: Summing the M characters of the even modulation subgroup annihilates entries except those with i≡j modulo M. Normalization |g|²=1/N gives diagonal k/2 and off-diagonal C_j/2 in M independent Hermitian two-coordinate blocks. Their eigenvalues give exactly the stated extrema, including the nonframe case. Half-shift conjugacy holds for w, and any unimodular sequence with this property is realizable with normalized phases w_j on the first half and 1 on the second. Vanishing moving sums is equivalent to invariance by shift k and a zero sum on a period d=gcd(N,k): subtract adjoining sums and then group their k summands into k/d periods. For odd k, d is odd and divides M, so conjugacy forces signs and prohibits zero mean with any flat phases. For even k and even M the alternating sign sequence works and a constant alphabet fails. For even k and odd M, d=2h, h=gcd(M,k/2) odd and M≡h mod 2h. Balance reduces to a sum of h real parts; binary signs cannot balance, ternary real parts 1 and −1/2 balance exactly with h/3 ones, and the conjugate halves consisting of i and −i always balance. All constructed sequences are realizable in the claimed alphabets, including the N=2 boundary and k=N. The supplied numerical comparison and finite search code were inspected, not executed; the universal result is analytic.
